subject: Dedicated reservation options & hot-standby/surge architectures for OpticScale
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@opticscale.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — sizing + hot-standby approach

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo this week. We liked the latency profiles and the fallback ideas for model variants. As we move toward a commercial commitment, procurement wants a clear set of dedicated reservation options that map to: (1) cluster size targets, (2) a minimum guaranteed GPU footprint, and (3) a ramp schedule with an explicit hot-standby / surge architecture for peak events.

High level context: OpticScale expects prod traffic to start low (L1 inference for narrow feature set) then ramp over 9 months to a steady state supporting ~120 concurrent sessions with 8k token avg sequences on weekdays. We need an option that minimizes cold-start risk during bursts and gives a predictable unit cost.

Can you send a concise menu of 2–3 reservation structures and recommended min GPUs, plus any warm-standby designs you’d propose? Procurement will also want a sample ramp calendar to include in the SOW.

Best,
Alex
Senior ML Infra, OpticScale

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — sizing + hot-standby approach

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a short proposal (v2) + a ramp workbook with scenario tabs. High-level options below; I'll drop into your calendar for a 30-min walk-through early next week.

Option A — Conservative steady:
- Cluster: 8 x A100 equivalent (shared across 2 model slots)
- Min guaranteed GPUs: 6 GPUs reserved (warm)
- Ramp: activate 2 GPUs/month for first 3 months, then reassess
- Hot-standby: 2 pre-warmed GPUs in the same region (warm KV cache), automatic scale to reserved pool on burst
- Use case: low initial traffic, tight cost control

Option B — Balanced ramp (recommended):
- Cluster: 12 x A100 equivalent
- Min guaranteed GPUs: 8 GPUs reserved
- Ramp: 4 GPUs after signing (30d), +2 GPUs at month 3, +2 GPUs at month 6
- Hot-standby: geo-fallback pair (secondary region standby) + 3 burst lanes for short spikes (shared burst pool)
- Use case: predictable headroom for marketing spikes and model experimentation

Option C — Growth-forward:
- Cluster: 20 x A100 equivalent
- Min guaranteed GPUs: 12 GPUs reserved
- Ramp: immediate 8 GPUs, +4 at month 2, +4 at month 4 (aggressive)
- Hot-standby: split active/standby across regions with warm prefix caching to reduce cold token cost
- Use case: teams that prioritize latency and minimal throttling

Attachments: opticscale_dedicated_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal summary), gpu_ramp_scenarios_opticscale.xlsx (workbook with utilization sims).

We included suggested SLA guardrails, warm-start credits for the first 30 days after each activation tranche, and a rollback plan to reduce reserved GPUs if utilization remains below thresholds after 60 days.

If you want, I can swap to a granular per-model lane instead of cluster-level lanes — that would increase predictability but adds management overhead.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Kim / team — quick technical notes to pair with the commercial options. I added a "hot-standby operational split" tab to the workbook. Key points: 

- Minimum GPU guidance: for 8k avg sequences and 120 concurrent sessions we estimate ~9–11 A100-equivalent GPUs sustained to meet 99th pct latency SLO with batching and KV caching. That aligns with Option B min=8 as a conservative reserved floor if you accept slightly longer tails during uncontested bursts.

- Warm vs. cold: keep at least 10% of the cluster fully warm (loaded KV caches and warmed kernel contexts). For Option B that means 1–2 GPUs constantly warm above reserved capacity in the burst pool to shave cold-start token latency.

- Surge design: prefer a hybrid approach — local burst lanes (shared among teammates, short TTL) + geo-standby for sustained overflow. Local burst = immediate low-latency but higher unit-cost; geo-standby = slower failover but cheaper for multi-hour surges.

- Autoscaling knobs: we recommend time-windowed burst throttles (5s smoothing) and a delta-capacity scheduler for gradual ramp activations to avoid noisy-scaling during marketing sends.

I left the workbook with a short sim showing cost delta between options at 30%, 60%, 90% utilization.

Ben
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood
[attachment: gpu_ramp_scenarios_opticscale.xlsx]

Alex — adding the commercial framing to Kimberly/Bens' technicals. Three commercial tiers mapped to the technical options above: 

- Tier 1 (Conservative): 12-month term, committed spend $45k/mo, includes 6 reserved GPUs baseline, 2 warm-standby GPUs included. Activation credit: 15% credit on first tranche. 30-day notice for down-scaling.

- Tier 2 (Balanced — recommended): 12-month term, committed spend $85k/mo, includes 8 reserved GPUs baseline, 3 burst lanes (pay-per-use beyond) and geo-standby. Activation credit: 30% credit on first tranche and 30 days of warm-start credits for each tranche. SLA: 99.5% region-level availability, 24/7 priority support.

- Tier 3 (Growth-forward): 24-month term, committed spend $150k/mo, includes 12 reserved GPUs baseline, priority capacity, and extended warm-start credits. 60-day activation smoothing window.

Ramp calendar (example for Tier 2):
- Day 0 (signing): deliver 4 GPUs in 30 days (warm)
- Month 3: +2 GPUs
- Month 6: +2 GPUs
- Month 9: review and optional +2 GPUs based on utilization

We can add contractual language for a 30-day activation SLA (Redwood commits to deliver new GPUs within the stated activation windows) and a single 30-day free warm-start credit after the first tranche to reduce your initial cost while we populate caches.

Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly / Karthik — procurement reviewed the Tier 2 commercial and the workbook. A few clarifications before we route to legal: 

1) Activation SLAs: we need the 30-day activation commitment in the SOW to include an explicit remediation if Redwood fails to deliver (e.g., pro-rated credit for days missed). Can you include sample language?

2) Warm-start credits: the 30-day warm-start credits per tranche look good. We request that the credits be applied automatically on invoice for the month the tranche is activated.

3) Minimum guaranteed GPUs: procurement requests the option for a 6-month freeze on down-scaling reductions after any activation tranche (to avoid premature cost volatility). Is that acceptable?

4) DocuSign: please send final proposal + SOW via DocuSign (we will countersign). We have one small ask — a 30-day activation credit (one-time) if we sign within 10 business days of receipt.

Please send updated proposal and a DocuSign link.
